thread:
sara.r: Heads-up 10: MetroTrust wants a BYOK POC next month. Requirements: HSM-backed keys, attestation report, enforced zero-key-exposure, and the ability to rotate CEKs every 6 hours. They also want evidence that keys never touch our host RAM.

bill.p: Do they require importing a CMK into our environment or keeping the master in their HSM and only doing wrap/unwrap calls? That decision changes our network & pricing.

eva.sec: Security note: MetroTrust asked for vendor attestation (CloudHSM or Thales) + signed attestation artifacts, plus signed timestamps for each rotation event. They also want dual-operator ceremony for initial key import and the ability to audit logs for 5 years.

tony.ops: From ops perspective, two options: (A) proxy wrap/unwrap to their HSM via PKCS#11 over a secured VPC peering (adds ~12-25ms per wrap); (B) accept imported wrapped CMKs and cache short-lived CEKs in TPM-backed enclaves. Option A minimizes key exposure risk. We'll need allowed CIDRs, throughput estimates, and cert bundles.

sara.r: MetroTrust explicitly says no plaintext keys on our nodes at any time. Can we guarantee that with Option A?

tony.ops: Yes. With Option A the master key never leaves their HSM. We request they generate ephemeral CEKs and return wrapped CEKs; our inference nodes call Unwrap only inside a secure PKCS#11 session that the customer's HSM controls. We'll provide a small agent that forwards requests; it never writes key material to disk or non-enclave memory.

eva.sec: I'll prepare the runbook template for the key ceremony and the attestation checklist. Also need to supply their compliance questionnaire answers.

bill.p: Pricing ballpark for presales: POC (3w): setup $6,000 (networking + agent dev), infra $3,000. Monthly estimated: 100 qps -> $12,000 SaaS + $2,000 HSM tunnel ops; 1,000 qps -> $55,000 SaaS + $9,000 ops. HSM attestation & signed-artifact package: one-time $12,000 + $1,500/mo for storage & audit support. Will confirm with finance.

security-bot: Auto-attach: "byok-attestation-checklist-v3.pdf" and "kek-ceremony-template.md".

eva.sec: MetroTrust also asked whether we can support split-key (threshold) HSM where key shares are held by two custodians. We can, but need to validate supported HSM vendor APIs and add ~2w of integration for the POC.

tony.ops: For the infra test plan, ask MetroTrust to provide: test vectors (plaintext->wrapped CEK), expected peak bursts, and a staging HSM endpoint with a cert we can validate. I'll draft a minimal curl example for their team:

curl -X POST https://kms-forwarder.redwood/internal/wrap \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <presales-token>" \
  -d '{"hsm_endpoint":"10.2.3.4:8443","key_label":"cust/kek/2026","plaintext_ce":"<base64>","ttl_sec":600}'

Response: {"wrapped_ce":"<base64>","wrap_meta":"sig,ts"}

sara.r: Next steps: Eva will produce the questionnaire responses + runbook draft by Wed EOD. Tony will assemble the curl & staging allowlist. Bill will update pricing and get an initial statement of work estimate. I'll book a 45m sync with MetroTrust for Tue next week to walk through the runbook. Any objections?

eva.sec: No objections 1: I'll include recommended retention and SIEM log formats.

tony.ops: No objections. I'll also spin up a minimal load script to show latency impact.

bill.p: Fine. Legal already pinged me: they flagged BYOK escrow (MetroTrust disallowed) and want to confirm data residency for audit logs. I'll coordinate once we have the runbook. :thumbsup:
